stem: A 1-year-old child re-presents after gastroenteritis with persistent vomiting, tachycardia and moderate dehydration despite an attempted oral fluid trial. What is the most appropriate fluid management?

options.text: Admit and continue oral fluids only

explanation: A child with ongoing vomiting, tachycardia and moderate dehydration after failed oral rehydration requires intravenous rehydration. Oral rehydration remains preferred when tolerated, but this child has failed that approach.

evidenceSources.title: Clinical Practice Guidelines: Gastroenteritis
evidenceSources.supports: Supports oral rehydration when tolerated and IV rehydration when oral rehydration fails or dehydration is significant.

evidenceSources.title: Clinical Practice Guidelines: Dehydration
evidenceSources.supports: Supports dehydration assessment and deficit plus maintenance fluid calculations.

evidenceSources.title: Clinical Practice Guidelines: Intravenous fluids
evidenceSources.supports: Supports isotonic bolus resuscitation and isotonic maintenance fluids with glucose and potassium when appropriate.
